title: [bot-alert/anomaly] Scanner anomalies 2026-09-15: phantom guard nondeterminism, round-trip profitability bug, scanner gaps, structural-field mismatch
body:
## Anomaly report — 2026-09-15 06:40 CDT (automated)

Generated by the scheduled anomaly-reporter workflow on 2026-09-15 06:40 America/Chicago. Source data: `logs/opportunities-2026-09-*.jsonl`, cross-checked against live RPC reads (block #93,831,122 and #93,831,144) on two independent endpoints.

---

### 1. Round-trip profitability bug — **CRITICAL, blocks all EXECUTE signals**

The scanner compares **one-way** `getAmountsOut` quotes on QuickSwap and SushiSwap for the same input. A spread between these one-way quotes does NOT imply an executable arbitrage, because both pools charge slippage on both legs.

I verified the recurring `WMATIC→USDC 20K → EXECUTE` signal on-chain (live, cross-checked on `primary` + `publicnode`):

| Size (WMATIC) | Leg1 QS→USDC | Leg2 SS→WMATIC | Gross WMATIC | Gross $ | Fee $ | Gas $ | **Net $** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|    200 |  19.18 | 198.91 | -1.09 | -0.11 | 0.01 | 0.02 | **-0.13** |
|   1000 |  95.89 | 992.59 | -7.41 | -0.71 | 0.05 | 0.02 | **-0.78** |
|  10000 | 956.19 | 9711.30 | -288.70 | -27.82 | 0.48 | 0.02 | **-28.32** |
|  20000 | 1906.29 | 18966.96 | -1033.04 | -99.55 | 0.96 | 0.02 | **-100.53** |

**Net is negative at every size from 200 to 20,000 WMATIC.** A live execution at 20K would burn ~$100 — the entire daily loss budget (`max_daily_loss_usd: 100`) in a single tx.

Root cause: the one-way comparison overstates profit because the SS pool's buy price at the trade margin is actually **higher** than QS's sell price. The pools' price bands overlap, so crossing both pools costs more than the spread at any size.

**Fix:** quote the actual round trip — `getAmountsOut(leg1_out, [tokenB, tokenA])` on the second DEX — and only signal EXECUTE when `roundTripOut > loan + aaveFee + gas`.

This explains the recurring WMATIC→USDC "EXECUTE" log entries on #76, #91, #102, etc.

---

### 2. Phantom guard nondeterminism — Sep 14 vs Sep 15, same pair flips classification

`WETH→USDC amount=10` produces essentially identical parameters on Sep 14 (04:56 UTC) and Sep 15 (04:57 UTC), but flip-flops between classification:

| Date | Spread % | Spread $ | Loan $ | Spread/Loan | Signal | `phantom` field |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 2026-09-14 | 28.93% | $7089 | $25139 | **28.2%** | **🟢 EXECUTE** | false |
| 2026-09-15 | 28.85% | $7032 | $24917 | **28.2%** | **👻 PHANTOM%** | false |

Both represent ~28% spread-to-loan ratios — far above the 5% phantom threshold. The Sep 14 classification (EXECUTE) is wrong; the Sep 15 classification (PHANTOM) is right. The guard appears to be firing nondeterministically.

On Sep 14, **every** pair was flagged EXECUTE, including `WETH→USDC amount=15` at **37.7% spread** and `WETH→WMATIC amount=10` at **22.4% spread**. On Sep 15 those same pairs all flip back to PHANTOM. That is a 5-for-5 misclassification on Sep 14.

---

### 3. Structured `phantom` / `isPhantom` fields always `false` — disagreements with signal label

Every record in the 2026-09-15 log with `signal: "👻 PHANTOM%"` still has `phantom: false` and `isPhantom: false` in the JSON body. The structured fields do not match the human-readable signal, so any downstream consumer filtering on `phantom === false` will silently include phantom-classified rows. This is how Sep 14's all-EXECUTE bug likely slipped through structural checks.

---

### 4. Scanner inactivity gaps — 4 missing days in September (27% miss rate)

Daily log files MISSING in 2026-09:

- 2026-09-05
- 2026-09-10
- 2026-09-13
- 2026-09-15 (Sep 15's run landed inside the 2026-09-14 file as an appended block — see `ts: 2026-09-15T04:57:51` entries. The dedicated daily file does not exist.)

4 of 15 expected day-files missing. The Sep 15 case is especially concerning: appended to yesterday's file because the file-naming convention uses file-creation date, not the `ts` field. That breaks any consumer that filters by filename.

---

### 5. No DAI phantom spreads or zero-liquidity pairs observed

For completeness: no DAI pairs appear in any 2026-09 opportunity log, and no records have `qsDepthUsd: 0` or `ssDepthUsd: 0`. The two watchlist items in this category are clear this month.

---

## Recommended actions

1. **Patch the scanner to quote round trips** (top — this is the difference between dry-run and live loss). One-way quotes should never emit EXECUTE.
2. **Audit the phantom guard** so it deterministically fires when `spreadUsd > 0.05 * loanNotionalUsd`. The Sep 14 mass-misfire suggests a numeric edge case or unit error.
3. **Write `phantom`/`isPhantom` from the same code path that sets the emoji signal** so they can never disagree.
4. **Filename convention:** use the `ts` date for the log filename, not file-creation time, so appended blocks land in the correct daily file. Investigate the weekday-Skipped pattern (Sep 5/10/13/15 are Fri/Wed/Sun/Tue — not a clean weekday pattern, so a CRON or runner hang is more likely than intentional filtering).
5. **Halt any automated live execution** until #1 lands. The current EXECUTE labels would currently burn the daily loss cap in a single tx.
